Designation.RegimeName: The Global Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Sanctions Regulations 2026
Designation.UKStatementofReasons: The Secretary of State considers that there are reasonable grounds to suspect that ARIEL RESIDENTIAL JUDEA AND SAMARIA LIMITED (hereafter “ARIEL RESIDENTIAL”) is an involved person under the Global Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Sanctions Regulations 2026 on the basis of the following grounds: (1) ARIEL RESIDENTIAL is or has been involved in facilitating or providing support for activity which constitutes a serious violation of international humanitarian law; (2) ARIEL RESIDENTIAL is or has been involved in profiting from activity which constitutes a serious violation of international humanitarian law. Specifically, ARIEL RESIDENTIAL is an Israeli property developer which initiates, plans, builds and markets housing in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, including at Ariel, Alei Zahav, Pedu’el, Metzad, and Efrat. The establishment and expansion of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank constitutes the transfer by Israel of parts of its own civilian population into the territory it occupies, contrary to Article 49(6) of the Fourth Geneva Convention, and a serious violation of international humanitarian law.

Designation.OtherInformation: Transport sanctions: Where transport sanctions apply, a ship owned, controlled, chartered or operated by a designated person is prohibited from entering a port in the UK, may be given a movement or a port entry direction, can be detained, and will be refused permission to register on the UK Ship Register or have its existing registration terminated. Similarly, an aircraft owned, chartered or operated by a designated person is prohibited from overflying or landing in the UK, may be given a movement direction, can be detained or moved to a specified airport, and will be refused permission to register on the CAA Aircraft Register or have its existing registration terminated. In addition to a prohibition of the provision of technical assistance relating to aircraft or ships will prevent a person from directly or indirectly providing technical assistance to, or for the benefit of, the designated person, where that technical assistance relates to an aircraft or ship.
Designation.UKStatementofReasons: The Secretary of State considers that there are reasonable grounds to suspect that Limited Liability Company LLC Vostok Oil is or has been involved in obtaining a benefit from or supporting the Government of Russia by carrying on business in a sector of strategic significance to the Government of Russia, namely the Russian energy sector.

Designation.OtherInformation:
Shipping sanctions: A specified ship must not be chartered or operated, is prohibited from being provided with access to or having its master or pilot cause it to enter a port in the UK, may have its registration on the UK Ship Register terminated, and a master or pilot of a specified ship may be given a port barring direction, a detention direction, and a port entry direction or a movement direction.
Trade sanctions: Where trade sanctions apply to a specified ship, it is an offence to directly or indirectly provide technical assistance, crew services, operating services, chartering services, brokering services, financial services or funds in relation to a specified ship. It is an offence to directly or indirectly provide services relating to the acquisition, sale, transfer or supply of a specified ship. It is also an offence to directly or indirectly procure services relating to a specified ship, including, in particular, services involving the use of that specified ship.
